chunks: In the narration of ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said:
"Whoever departs from ʿArafāt with the people, then does not remain with them at Jamʿ and goes on to Minā deliberately or out of disregard, then a badanah is incumbent upon him."

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: departed from ʿArafāt along with the pilgrims
key_terms.بِجَمْعٍ: at Jamʿ, meaning Muzdalifah, where the pilgrim must stay
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: the plain of ʿArafāt, a principal station of hajj
key_terms.مُسْتَخِفًّا: out of disregard or taking the matter lightly
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the ritual site to which pilgrims proceed after Jamʿ

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who skips staying at Jamʿ (Muzdalifah) during hajj and goes directly to Minā?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the rites of hajj, specifically the obligation of remaining at Jamʿ after departing from ʿArafāt. It states that whoever intentionally or dismissively skips this required standing and proceeds to Minā must offer a badanah as expiation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2990 - In a narration from Ali ibn Ri'ab, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Whoever departs from Arafat with the people but does not stay with them at Jam‘ (Muzdalifah) and deliberately or out of disregard proceeds directly to Mina, must offer a badnah (a camel as expiation)."
